applied.problem: Too absolute: a very light differential winding keeps the speed almost constant (the lesson's own explain), and a speed that rises with load can also come from interpole polarity, brushes off neutral or armature reaction, so 'is unstable' and 'is opposing' overstate.

'Starts hard like a series motor' contradicts the lesson's own ranking and picture (series 4.00, compound 2.30, shunt 2.00 at twice rated current); and the 22.4% rise is from rated load with 15% of the full-load field, which the sentence leaves out.

'Safe light while the shunt field is connected' needs full field: the practice itself warns a weakened shunt field gives a very high no-load speed; 'dip a little' undersells a 15-30% droop; and the same maker's about 30% is dropped from 'typical real figures'.

Screen 4's 'safe to run light while the shunt field is connected' needs full field (screen 5: weakening it gives very high no-load speeds); screen 6's 'the speed rises with load' is too sure, as a very light reversed series winding only flattens it.
The starting-torque ranking holds at the same current; stated flatly it overreaches, since sources differ on a shunt motor's starting torque (lesson 7's contested point).
